rules.statement: A database migration must only expand the schema (add tables, nullable or defaulted columns, and indexes) so the previous release keeps working against it; drops, renames, and tightened constraints go in a later release that is explicitly marked as a contract step.
rules.why: The previous release keeps serving while the migration runs and during the rollout, and a rollback returns to it without reversing the migration, so a schema it cannot read breaks production.
rules.check: Look for migrations that drop or rename tables/columns, make a column non-nullable, add a column that is non-nullable with no default, or add a constraint to an existing table, and are not marked as a deliberate contract step.

rules.statement: Rename a column or table as an add, a data copy, and a later drop spread across at least two releases, never as a single rename operation.
rules.why: A rename in one step breaks the previous release that still reads the old name during rollout and after a rollback.
rules.check: Look for RenameColumn/RenameTable (or equivalent raw SQL) in a migration, or an add-and-drop of the same data in the same migration.

rules.statement: Review raw SQL in a migration (migrationBuilder.Sql) by hand for drops, renames, or tightened constraints, because automated expand-only checks do not classify it.
rules.why: Raw SQL bypasses the test that catches contracting schema operations, so it stays a review item.
rules.check: Any migrationBuilder.Sql call whose SQL contains DROP, RENAME, ALTER ... SET NOT NULL, or ADD CONSTRAINT on an existing table, with no contract-step marking.

rules.statement: Do not put long-running data migrations in a schema migration; run them in application code after the rollout.
rules.why: The migration runs as a pre-upgrade step that blocks the release and must fit inside the deployment timeout.
rules.check: Look for migrations that backfill or transform large amounts of data (bulk UPDATE/INSERT ... SELECT, loops over rows) rather than only changing schema.

rules.statement: Run a database migration Job as a Helm pre-install/pre-upgrade hook that is at least as restricted as the server pod: non-root user, read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, and automountServiceAccountToken false.
rules.why: A failed migration should fail the release before any pod is replaced, and the migration Job must not run with more privilege than the server.
rules.check: In chart templates, check that a migration Job has the pre-install,pre-upgrade hook annotation and a securityContext with runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop ALL, and no mounted service-account token.

rules.statement: Give a migration Job's pod an app.kubernetes.io/component label different from the server pods, and make Service and PodDisruptionBudget selectors include the server component so they never select the Job.
rules.why: A Service or PodDisruptionBudget that matches the migration pod would route traffic to it or count it toward availability.
rules.check: Check that Service/PDB selectors include app.kubernetes.io/component for the server, and the Job pod template uses a different component value.

rules.statement: Let the migration database connection be configured separately from the runtime connection, defaulting to the runtime one, so the running application can run without rights to change its own schema.
rules.why: Keeping schema-change rights apart from runtime rights means a compromised or buggy host cannot change its schema.
rules.check: Look for migration workers or charts that hard-wire the runtime connection string or secret with no separate, overridable migration connection setting.
